faqs.question: Where is the Faculty of Business Studies and Finance located?
faqs.answer: The faculty is located at the Kuliyapitiya premises of Wayamba University of Sri Lanka (60200, Kuliyapitiya, Sri Lanka).

faqs.question: When was the faculty established?
faqs.answer: The Faculty of Business Studies and Finance (FBSF) was established on 01 October 1999 by the Government Notification in the Extraordinary Gazette No. 1093/8 of Tuesday, 17 August 1999, and remains the fastest growing faculty of Wayamba University of Sri Lanka.

faqs.question: How many departments does the faculty have?
faqs.answer: The faculty consists of four departments of studies: Department of Accountancy, Department of Banking and Finance, Department of Business Management, and Department of Insurance and Valuation.

faqs.question: What are the admission requirements for the Diploma in Accounting Information Systems (DAIS)?
faqs.answer: Any one of the following: passed G.C.E Advanced Level in any stream; passed AAT second Level; passed ICASL executive Level; passed CIMA 1st Level; passed CMA 1st Level; passed ACCA 1st Level. Other qualifications may be acceptable case by case subject to approval of the Board of Study. Lectures are held on weekends.

faqs.question: What are the admission routes for the Diploma in Banking and Financial Studies (DBFS)?
faqs.answer: (1) Passed G.C.E (A/L) examination in any stream in a single attempt; (2) Six passes in G.C.E (O/L) Examination in one sitting with three credits and two years working experience in a reputed institution; (3) Any other qualification with two years working experience, considered case by case by the Board of Study and the Senate of WUSL. A good knowledge of English and performance at the admission test/interview are required.

faqs.question: How does the PGDBM lead to the MBA?
faqs.answer: The Postgraduate Diploma in Business Management (PGDBM) runs for one academic year with twelve compulsory course modules (24 credits) plus a project report. Those who complete all PGDBM requirements may be admitted to the second year — the Masters Degree in Business Administration (MBA) — earning 16 credits through two taught courses (8 credits) and a comprehensive research thesis (8 credits). A limited number of direct-entrance candidates may also be admitted to the MBA.

faqs.question: How do I submit a research paper to the Journal of Accountancy and Finance (JAF)?
faqs.answer: Submit the full paper (maximum 30 pages, B5 size, MS Word format) to jaf@wyb.ac.lk. Papers must contain Title, Abstract, Keywords, Introduction, Literature Review, Methodology, Results and Discussion, Conclusion and References. The acceptable similarity index is up to 20 percent.

options.fqac_structure:
FQAC coordinates quality assurance aspects with the Quality Assurance Units of its four academic departments (Department of Accountancy, Department of Banking & Finance, Department of Business Management, Department of Insurance & Valuation).
FQAC facilitates programme reviews of the four academic departments of the Faculty.
FQAC comprises a committee of academic staff members chaired by the Dean of the Faculty and is coordinated by an appointed Faculty Coordinator.
FQAC plans, implements and evaluates quality assurance activities and gives direction on best practices among staff and students of the faculty in liaison with other related committees within the Faculty (Curriculum and Academic Development Committee, Research and Higher Degree Committee, Teaching and Learning Committee, Student-Staff Liaison Committee, etc.)
options.fqac_functions: The ultimate intention of FQAC is to strengthen the Faculty’s capacity and commitment to produce quality graduates in the disciplines of Accountancy & Business Finance, Banking & Finance, Business Management and Insurance & Finance.

departments.title: Department of Accountancy
departments.excerpt: Pioneers of business education at Wayamba University
departments.content: The Department of Accountancy at Wayamba University of Sri Lanka has played a pioneering role in business education since the establishment of the University in 2001, being one of the earliest academic disciplines introduced. At present, the Department offers the B.Sc in Accountancy and Business Finance degree, designed to meet the evolving demands of the accounting and business environment. The degree programme is structured into three key academic clusters — Accountancy, Business Finance, and Accounting Information Systems — designed to provide students with a comprehensive and industry-relevant education.

meta.hod_title: Message from the Head of the Department
meta.hod_message: The Department is strongly committed to delivering high-quality accounting education with a holistic approach to developing competent and ethical business professionals. Our academic staff comprise well-qualified scholars with doctoral training, relevant industry experience, and professional credentials in accountancy and related fields. They actively engage in research across diverse areas, including financial and management accounting, auditing, financial management, accounting education, taxation, and corporate governance. Our teaching and learning practices emphasize strong theoretical foundations, professional competencies, and innovative pedagogical approaches. The accounting programmes offered by the Department are accredited by leading professional bodies such as the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants (CIMA), the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (CA Sri Lanka), and the Institute of Certified Management Accountants (CMA). These accreditations enhance the professional recognition and career prospects of our graduates. Graduates of the Department are well prepared to serve in managerial and professional capacities across a wide range of organizations, including accounting and auditing firms, financial institutions, corporate entities, government bodies, and non-profit organizations, both in Sri Lanka and beyond.
meta.research: Academic staff actively engage in research across diverse areas, including financial and management accounting, auditing, financial management, accounting education, taxation, and corporate governance. The department publishes the Journal of Accountancy & Finance (JAF) and the open-access Journal of SACFIRE, and participates in the SACFIRE symposium and the faculty-level JARSYM journal.

departments.title: Department of Banking and Finance
departments.excerpt: Pioneer in banking and finance education in Sri Lanka
departments.content: The Department of Banking & Finance is one of the pioneer academic departments in the Faculty of Business Studies and Finance, which offers the B.Sc Banking and Finance (Special) degree programme every year to the undergraduates of the faculty since 2001. The Department of Banking and Finance is committed to providing a well-rounded banking and finance education and co-curricular experience to all its students. The department is basically focused on the subject areas of Economics, Bank Management, Investments, Financial Markets and Institutions. The primary focus of the department is to enhance undergraduate and postgraduate learning and knowledge by teaching particularly in Banking & Finance and technology, and in close association with industry and commerce.

meta.hod_title: Message from the Head of the Department
meta.hod_message: The Department of Banking & Finance is the pioneer department to offer a specialized degree in Banking & Finance in Sri Lanka. Bachelor of Science (Special) Degree in Banking & Finance is a four-year duration programme conducted in English medium offered with the objective of providing a sound academic & professional background in Banking & Finance enabling the graduates to learn a wide array of subjects from the areas of Banking & Finance. The department is offering students an outcome-based education through outcome-based teaching and learning process to develop their personal capabilities, discipline-specific competencies, professional, ethical and social attributes in order to become a skilled graduate who can compete in the global context. The department focuses on the holistic development of undergraduates by a combination of both curricular and extracurricular activities. Apart from the curriculum, the department provides the opportunity for students to follow several certificate courses developed to improve their soft skills, language fluency and research competencies. The department has partnered with many reputed banks and financial institutions enabling students to gain the opportunity to expose to real-world, by completing a comprehensive internship programme of six months during the degree programme. The department staff comprises many PhD qualified academics and well-experienced staff in the discipline of Banking & Finance. The entire fraternity of the Department of Banking & Finance cohesively works and commits towards the accomplishment of its mission of achieving excellence as a department in the arena of Banking and Finance.

departments.title: Department of Insurance and Valuation
departments.excerpt: Pioneer academic center in risk and insurance education
departments.content: The Department of Insurance and Valuation is committed to enhance the education in the field of Insurance and Finance by introducing undergraduate, diploma and higher diploma programmes with skills, capabilities and competencies to meet the real world requirement through interaction with public and private sector organizations. It is also committed to pursuing the excellence in teaching and learning in Insurance and Finance by conducting research and community service while making all efforts to contribute to the vision of the Faculty of Business Studies and Finance. At present, the Department is successfully conducting undergraduate, Higher Diploma, Diploma, and Certificate programmes for internal and external students, and planned to commence the postgraduate degree programme specific to Risk Management and Insurance.

programmes.title: Postgraduate Diploma in Business Management (PGDBM)
programmes.excerpt: One-year postgraduate diploma with twelve taught modules and a project report, leading to the MBA.
programmes.content: The Postgraduate Diploma in Business Management (PGDBM) is a programme of study which will run through one academic year (approximately one calendar year duration). Participants will follow twelve course modules during the period, of which all course modules will be compulsory. Each course module will be of about 30 hours of teaching. The academic year comprises two terms; twelve courses are taught during this period. In addition, every participant should complete a project report and submit the same at the end of the 2nd term of the Programme. Those who complete all the requirements of the PGDBM may be admitted to the 2nd year of the Programme — the Masters Degree in Business Administration.

programmes.title: Diploma in Banking and Financial Studies (DBFS)
programmes.excerpt: One-year external diploma (30 credits, SLQF Level 3) designed to meet the demands of the flourishing banking and financial sector.
programmes.content: Today, the banking and financial sector is flourishing in our country and requires more employees and professionals to meet the demand. Having identified the expected qualities and competencies required for the financial sector, the Department of Banking and Finance — the pioneer in banking and finance education provider in Sri Lanka — has designed its external programmes to cope up with the challenge. The Diploma in Banking and Financial Studies (DBFS) facilitates learning in theory and practices to improve skills in advanced areas of economics, banking and finance and equips students with an integrated approach to managerial skills. The course units are designed to develop analytical, problem-solving and decision-making abilities, awareness of domestic and international economics and financial environment.

programmes.title: Advanced Certificate in Financial Services Management (ACFSM)
programmes.excerpt: First advanced certificate programme of its nature offered by the department under its external programmes (SLQF Level 2).
programmes.content: The Department of Banking and Finance is one of the prominent departments in the Sri Lankan university system to cater needs of the Banking & financial industry. The introduction of this nature of course was a long-felt need of the Industry as there are no advanced certificate programmes offered by any university related to this discipline. Further, many employees in the banking and financial services sector are engaged in their work without theoretical background related to their employment. The Department of Banking and Finance considered this vacuum and decided to introduce this Advanced Certificate programme with the aim of infusing enthusiasm among potential people who are eager to solve problems they encountered while in the service. This is the first Advanced Certificate programme introduced by the Department of this nature under its external programmes. Financial firms, on the other hand, could monitor this programme and embody this into their promotion schemes too. The programme is designed following the requirements of the Sri Lanka Qualification Framework (SLQF) Level 2.

journals.title: Journal of Annual Research Symposium in Management (JARSYM)
journals.content: A publication of Students' Research of the Annual Research Symposium in Management. The Journal of ARSYM (JARSYM) is a refereed journal published bi-annually by the Faculty of Business Studies & Finance, Wayamba University of Sri Lanka. The aim of the JARSYM is to disseminate high-quality research findings on a variety of timely topics generated by undergraduate researchers at the Wayamba University of Sri Lanka. Furthermore, it opens up avenues for undergraduates involved in the industry to share their inventions, state-of-the-art discoveries, and novel ideas. The main philosophy behind the JARSYM is to enhance the research culture within the faculty, thereby within Wayamba University. All research articles submitted are double-blind reviewed prior to publishing. Views expressed in the research articles are not the views of the Faculty of Business Studies and Finance, Wayamba University of Sri Lanka, or the Editorial Board.

journals.title: Journal of Accountancy and Finance (JAF)
journals.content: The Journal of Accountancy and Finance is biannually published by the Department of Accountancy, Faculty of Business Studies and Finance, Wayamba University of Sri Lanka. The main objective of the journal is to publish scientific research findings that address issues and development related to the Accounting and Finance Industry, particularly at both the national and international levels. Initially issued as an Accountancy Journal for six volumes since July 2004; in 2014 the journal was renamed the Journal of Accountancy and Finance and recognized as a refereed journal, published biannually. The journal provides a worthwhile platform for academics spread out within the country as well as globally to publish their novel research work in the field of Accountancy and Finance.

journals.title: Sri Lankan Journal of Business Studies and Finance (SLJBSF)
journals.content: The Sri Lankan Journal of Business Studies and Finance (SLJBSF) is a double-blind peer-reviewed scholarly journal which aims to publish scholarly work in the field of Business Studies & Finance. It is published semi-annually by the Faculty of Business Studies and Finance, Wayamba University of Sri Lanka. The objectives of the SLJBSF are three folds: (i) to benchmark the Faculty’s contribution for the growth of the body of knowledge in Business Studies & Finance; (ii) to promote and provide convenient access to publish and disseminate the research works of potential researchers/scholars; and (iii) to maintain the Faculty journal as an updated channel to provide solutions for unsolved problems while maintaining academic excellence in knowledge dissemination in the field. The journal is addressed to diverse communities, including academics, professionals, graduate and postgraduate students, and anyone with a keen interest in the field of Business Studies & Finance. The Faculty planned to publish Volume I, Issue I of SLJBSF in March 2021.

journals.content: The Sri Lankan Journal of Banking and Finance (SLJBF) is an official double-blind peer-reviewed journal that publishes research papers and scholarly work by the Department of Banking and Finance, Wayamba University of Sri Lanka. journals.title: Voice of Insurance
journals.content: The Voice of Insurance is the biannual specialized magazine published by the Department of Insurance and Valuation of the Wayamba University of Sri Lanka. The Voice of Insurance provides a trustful and independent information platform for the stakeholders of the risk & insurance business in Sri Lanka. The magazine aims to enlighten the sphere of risk and insurance with its latest trends, information, strategies, and insights to mitigate the dynamism of the business environment. Even though there are many institutions and professionals connected to the risk & insurance business, there is no common platform to present their professional voices, information, experience, and expectations; the Voice of Insurance aims to fill that gap by connecting the stakeholders in the insurance business in Sri Lanka and expects to create a trustful information source for the industry.

A leading faculty in business studies and finance at Wayamba University of Sri Lanka.

The Faculty of Business Studies and Finance (FBSF) is one of the academic faculties of Wayamba University of Sri Lanka, offering undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma and external programmes across accountancy, banking and finance, business management, and insurance and valuation. The faculty is committed to excellence in teaching, research and industry engagement.
Established in 1999, the faculty continues to build tomorrow’s business and finance leaders through quality education and research that connects academia with industry.
All deadlines and events listed are historical and retained for reference.
Contact the faculty office for programme enquiries, applications and general information.
History, vision, mission and the leadership of the Faculty of Business Studies and Finance.

The Faculty of Business Studies and Finance was established in 1999 as an academic faculty of Wayamba University of Sri Lanka. It was established by the Government Notification in the Extraordinary Gazette No. 1093/8 of Tuesday, 17 August 1999, and commenced operations on 01 October 1999.

The faculty offers a range of undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma and external programmes across four academic departments: Accountancy, Banking & Finance, Business Management, and Insurance & Valuation.

The Faculty Quality Assurance Cell (FQAC) coordinates quality assurance activities for the faculty in liaison with the Centre for Quality Assurance (CQA) of the university, working with the Quality Assurance Units of the four academic departments.
The faculty operates a number of standing committees that oversee curriculum, research, teaching and learning, and student–staff liaison.
Contact the faculty office for programme enquiries, applications and general information.
Four academic departments offering undergraduate, postgraduate, diploma and external programmes.

The faculty offers 10 academic programmes across the four departments — undergraduate degrees, diplomas, higher diplomas, advanced certificates and external programmes. Use the programme directory to explore categories, departments and course structures.

The faculty promotes research that connects academia with industry. Faculty members publish in refereed journals, present at annual research symposia, and engage with professional bodies and industry partners.
Research areas include accounting, banking, finance, insurance, valuation, risk management, business management, entrepreneurship and digital transformation.
